exclusions.name: obr.housing_benefit
exclusions.reason: Frame-side gap, not a weight question, decomposed on 2026-09-16 (spine-q design weights unless stated). FRS 2024-25 reports 1.56m Housing Benefit benefit units, 99.9 percent renters, near the DWP GB caseload (1.94m in January 2025 falling to 1.46m by December); the spine carries 1.21m GB reporters (GBP 7.15bn reported) because the SPI support channel re-imputes benefit receipt onto its synthetic households without tenure coherence: 363k of its 449k reporting units sit in owner-occupied households and can never be paid. The engine then pays Housing Benefit only to reporting units with a rented tenure, not drawn into Universal Credit, under the capital limit and carrying the household's rent (rent is the household head's benefit unit's alone; claims_all_entitled_benefits collapses to a scalar, so there is no take-up lever): 407k all-pension-age reporting units were drawn into Universal Credit by the 55 percent take-up draw although they cannot claim it, and the working-age remainder is pared by the means test. On the Q50f candidate the engine pays 235k units and GBP 2.13bn against the OBR GBP 12.10bn (-82 percent); the U8 lever receipt already showed the same lever from the other side (0.85 take-up moved this row from -0.0 to -52.4 percent). This PR gates the draw to units with an adult under State Pension age; the SPI-channel tenure defect is a #840/#145 item; the OBR line also carries supported and temporary accommodation the frame has no concept for. Re-measured on every evaluation with the three Housing Benefit caseload rows; renew or retire on the next spine that carries the SPI repair.
exclusions.adjudication: microcosm#882 (re-adjudication on the 2026-09-16 mechanism receipts: tools/diagnose_uk_legacy_benefits.py on spine-q, the Q50f candidate and FRS 2024-25, recorded in experiments/882-uc-repairs-receipts.md; the #882 status comment of 2026-09-16; María's sign-off in review of the #882 repairs PR)

exclusions.reason: Frame-side gap, not a weight question, decomposed on 2026-09-16. FRS 2024-25 reports 63k JSA benefit units at design weights (37k contributory, 23k income-based; 27 records), so the source reproduces the DWP count. The spine carries 178k contributory and 92k income-based reporters (GB, design weights) because the SPI support channel re-imputes benefit receipt onto its synthetic households: 161k of the 181k contributory reporters sit there. The stage-6 legacy_jobseeker_proxy (967k) is consumed by nothing. On the Q50f candidate the row measures 34k against 71,000 (-52 percent) after the solve pares the reporters to fit the OBR JSA spend line. The repair is the SPI channel's benefit-receipt fill (#840/#145), not a JSA rule; the income-based reporters are a legacy-scheme residual DWP no longer counts. Renew or retire on the next spine that carries the SPI repair.
exclusions.adjudication: microcosm#882 (re-adjudication on the 2026-09-16 mechanism receipts: tools/diagnose_uk_legacy_benefits.py on spine-q, the Q50f candidate and FRS 2024-25, recorded in experiments/882-uc-repairs-receipts.md; the #882 status comment of 2026-09-16; María's sign-off in review of the #882 repairs PR)

exclusions.name: dwp.uc.households_housing_element
exclusions.reason: Structural bias, not a weight question: DWP's any-tenure housing-entitlement count is social plus private plus 'Other or unknown' tenure, and the model has no other/unknown tenure (uc_housing_costs_element pays only council, housing-association and private renters), so the model's any-tenure count is identically the social plus private rows, which are bound and fit; the row overstates the reachable total by the other/unknown cell, 112,518 of 4,037,650 in calendar 2025 (2.8 percent; the published any-tenure mean, which the three tenure cells reproduce to the unit). Fitting all three housing rows would ask the solver to over-fill the tenure rows by that amount. Measured on every evaluation as the housing-element caseload diagnostic (Q50f -0.8 percent, D2 +0.6 percent at the baseline).
exclusions.adjudication: microcosm#882 (element sizing at the 10 September 2026 baseline, docs/uk-uc-baseline-2026-09-10.md; María's sign-off in review of microcosm#921 on 2026-09-15, setting the one-month window)
